# Draft:Edward V. Ciampi

----
Edward V. Ciampi is an American local politician and business executive who serves as the District 5 commissioner and vice chair of the Martin County Board of County Commissioners. He represents western Martin County, including Palm City and part of Indiantown, and has been elected multiple times to the commission as a member of the Republican Party. Outside public office, Ciampi is vice president of sales and international development at Chicago Stainless Equipment, a Palm City–based manufacturer of industrial pressure and temperature gauges.
Career
Business career
Ciampi has spent much of his career in the private sector. By 2015 he was serving as vice president of sales and international development at Chicago Stainless Equipment Inc., a Palm City manufacturer of temperature and pressure gauges. A 2020 profile by Treasure Coast Business described the company as an 80-year-old manufacturer of industrial pressure and temperature gauges used in food and beverage, pet-food and pharmaceutical industries, and identified Ciampi as its vice president of sales.
In an interview with the Business Development Board of Martin County, Ciampi stated that he heads international sales and international development for Chicago Stainless Equipment and has traveled to nearly 30 countries in that role. He has spoken about export practices at events such as “Export University 101,” organized by the Business Development Board in partnership with state and federal trade agencies.
Martin County Commission
Ciampi was first elected to the Martin County Commission in 2008 and represented District 5 through 2012. According to a 2015 TCPalm election article, he left the commission in 2012 to make an unsuccessful run for Martin County clerk of the circuit court.
In 2015 Ciampi announced a campaign to “recapture” the District 5 seat, positioning himself as a Republican candidate who sought to bridge what he described as a divide between “pro-growth” and “slow-growth” factions on the commission. In August 2016 he won election to the District 5 commission seat, returning to the board after a four-year absence.
As of 2025, official county records list Ciampi as the District 5 commissioner and vice chair of the Martin County Board of County Commissioners, with a term of office from 2024 to 2028. District 5 covers western Martin County, including Palm City and parts of Indiantown. The county property appraiser and supervisor of elections similarly list him as the incumbent commissioner for District 5.
Ciampi has also held leadership and liaison roles on county and regional boards. Martin County’s commission-representation roster for 2025 lists him as a member or alternate on bodies including the county’s affordable-housing task team, the Business Development Board of Martin County, the Indian River Lagoon Council (as an alternate) and transportation and regional planning councils. He has served as chair and vice chair of the Martin County Commission in different years, and as vice chair of the Martin Metropolitan Planning Organization policy board.
2024 election
In the 2024 election cycle, Ciampi ran for another four-year term representing District 5. A pre-primary profile by radio station WJNO noted that he faced two Republican challengers in an open primary that was available to all county voters because no Democratic or third-party candidates qualified for the seat.
According to election results summarized by local outlet TreasureCoast.com, Ciampi won the District 5 county commission race with 41.51% of the vote in the 2024 primary, ahead of challengers in the three-way contest. BallotReady, a nonpartisan voter-information service, lists him as holding the Martin County Commission District 5 seat through December 31, 2028.
Political positions and issues
Coverage of Ciampi’s campaigns and commission service has frequently focused on growth management and development in Martin County. In his 2015 campaign launch, he said he hoped to “bridge the gap” between the county’s “pro-growth” and “slow-growth” blocs and to focus on projects that could win unanimous support from the five-member commission. Reporting on the 2024 District 5 race by TCPalm described growth and development as the top issue for Ciampi and his challengers.
As a commissioner, Ciampi has also commented publicly on housing affordability and land-use regulation. In 2025 local television coverage quoted him as saying that Martin County lacked sufficient affordable housing options and that “to do nothing” about the issue would be irresponsible for elected officials, in the context of discussions about guest-home rentals and growth regulations.
Personal life
Ciampi is married to his wife, Liz, and the couple live in Palm City, Florida. A 2015 profile noted that they have three children. County and regional directories also list his residence in western Martin County and identify him as a local business executive as well as an elected official.
